brief: A GS trading desk note frames an overnight Asia selloff (KOSPI -5-6%, Nikkei -1.5-2%, memory names down 7-10% on CXMT news) as concentrated in five Nikkei stocks rather than indiscriminate, calling it an unwind of crowded AI/semis positioning rather than wholesale selling. Within AI, the author argues Microsoft's Maia 300 hurts NVDA but helps custom silicon, Broadcom and Intel reaffirmed demand through 2030, and Meta's Muse Wonder adds frontier competition; he concludes competition raises aggregate compute demand, so the real risk is capacity/power delivery, which is de-rating capex stocks. The broader market rotation (long AI, short everything else unwinding into bonds, gold, equal-weight and Russell) stems from investors protecting a strong year's gains amid crowded books. Separately, a Russia-Ukraine ceasefire collapsed within hours and Houthi strikes hit Riyadh, yet Brent stayed lower because the market is pricing escalation differently from actual lost barrels, a fragile distinction. Since aggregate equity exposure and nets stay conservative, he calls this rotation rather than liquidation, expects hyperscalers and bought dips in hardware, and flags financials as a possible extension of the rotation.
